text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- The next 24 hours could bring aftershocks in the wake of Wednesday's tremor.
- A solution to the Cyprus problem will be attempted if President Clinton wins second term, according to a senior presidential aide.
CYPRUS MAIL
- Strong quake rocks the island. Buildings were damaged, roads were closed by landslides and over 100 aftershocks were reported.
- Joint military manoeuvres end with new F-16 fly-past at parade.
- Police were paid for time they did not work, says the justice minister.
- The United Nations are to intervene as Turks block replacement of Greek Cypriot teacher in Karpasia.
HARAVGHI
- The House of Representatives want legislation for the operation of TV and radio stations by the summer.
- Britain has a plan on security issues in Cyprus.
- Cleaners at Larnaca hospital say they will step up industrial action over recruitment.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- Earthquake rocks Cyprus. Limited damage has been reported because of the depth of the epicentre.
- Nikiforos military exercise gives a show of strength.
- The Democratic Party and the Democratic Rally parties are nearing agreement on cooperating during December's municipal elections.
SIMERINI
- Cyprus lives hours of terror and anxiety after earthquake.
- Greek wings covered Cyprus during Nikiforos exercise.
- The island's defence fund will gain an additional 35 million pounds if public defence contribution is increased by one percent.
